st.headline: Visa approved to prepare domestic payments business in China
st.teaser: Visa’s clearance of the regulatory hurdle will allow it to operate in China’s US$144 trillion payments market.
fullText: BEIJING – Visa received approval to begin preparations to establish a domestic bank card clearing business in China, as the firm follows rivals Mastercard and American Express in serving the country’s massive payments market.

“We greatly appreciate the important role of the leaders of the United States and China in pursuing a constructive and strategically stable relationship between the world’s largest economies,” Visa chief executive officer Ryan McInerney said in the statement.
The company’s Beijing unit won the greenlight from the People’s Bank of China, the official Xinhua News Agency reported on Oct 13.
It must complete preparatory work within one year before applying to commence operations and obtaining the clearing business licence, Xinhua added.
Visa’s clearance of the regulatory hurdle will allow it to operate in China’s US$144 trillion (S$184 trillion) payments market and marks the end to its years-long pursuit.
Visa applied for the licence in 2017, local media reported.

Competitor Mastercard received approval to establish its bank card clearing business in 2020, and Amex’s joint venture in the country was approved to start bank card clearing services several months after that.
For years, the battle for entry into mainland China’s massive domestic clearing market was a primary friction point in the broader trade dispute between the world’s two largest economies.
Earlier in 2026, US President Donald Trump said he brought up Visa’s request for access to mainland China’s market during a meeting with Xi Jinping in Beijing .
Visa’s CEO McInerney accompanied Trump on that May trip to China.
Xi later met his counterpart in Washington in late September, with both agreeing on a trade truce extension .
The two are scheduled to talk again in person on the sidelines of the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen in November.
China first signalled an opening in the sector in June 2015, announcing that foreign bank-card clearing providers could apply for licences by establishing local units or through acquisitions.
The move was designed to dismantle the long-standing monopoly held by state-run China UnionPay.
While the approval marks a significant milestone, Visa is entering a market that looks very different from the one it first sought to enter.

China’s payments ecosystem is now dominated by domestic mobile platforms Alipay and WeChat Pay, which have largely bypassed traditional card networks and become the primary channels for everyday transactions.
China had 10.2 billion bank cards in circulation at the end of 2025, with transaction value totalling 963.6 trillion yuan (S$184 trillion) in 2025, according to the People’s Bank of China. BLOOMBERG

cna.headline: India youth protest leaders detained after entering barricaded Delhi protest site
cna.teaser: The detentions on Tuesday (Oct 13) came after Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders entered Jantar Mantar, an iconic site for demonstrations that police had removed from New Delhi's list of designated protest venues a day earlier.
fullText: NEW DELHI: India's youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) said on Tuesday (Oct 13) that key leaders had been detained after entering an iconic protest site in New Delhi blocked by police. Opposition parties and supporters of the movement have taken to the streets in recent days, defying a security clampdown to demand the resignation of the head of India's election commission, accusing it of manipulating voter rolls to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling party. The Election Commission of India, which oversees the voting process in the world's most populous nation, has denied any wrongdoing. Delhi Police said on Monday that Jantar Mantar in the heart of the capital had been taken off the list of designated official protest sites. The site has been sealed off for several days by yellow metal barricades and guarded by a heavy police presence . But a video posted online by CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke showed protesters clambering over the barricades, before running into the empty space and waving the national flag - before police chased and detained them. "CJP sneaks inside to reclaim Jantar Mantar," the group said in a post on social media, adding that those detained included leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Ajinkya Shinde. "All of them have been detained by Delhi Police," it added.

Delhi Police had announced three official sites on Monday as alternatives to Jantar Mantar, where protesters have gathered for decades - including CJP demonstrations that led to India's education minister, Dharmendra Pradhan, stepping down over an examination scandal in July. "You cannot denotify the resistance," Dipke said, tagging Modi in his post. Modi, in comments at a business conference in New Delhi on Tuesday, called India the "mother of democracy", but did not refer directly to the protests. "In our country, people openly debate a wide range of issues and discuss different perspectives," he said.
